511:             if let Some(name) = extract_func_name(operand, source) {
512:                 if name == "isempty" {
513:                     // Check if the argument to isempty is strfind(...)
514:                     if let Some(args_node) = find_arguments(operand) {
515:                         if let Some(first_arg) = first_named_child(args_node) {
516:                             if first_arg.kind() == "function_call" {
517:                                 if let Some(inner_name) = extract_func_name(first_arg, source) {
518:                                     if inner_name == "strfind" {
519:                                         diags.push(make_diag("STCCS", node));
520:                                     }
521:                                 }
522:                             }
523:                         }
524:                     }
525:                 }
526:             }
527:         }
528: 
529:         diags
530:     }

536:     /// File-level check for array/struct growth inside loops.
537:     fn check_growth_in_loops(
538:         &self,
539:         tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
540:         source: &str,
541:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
542:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
543:         let root = tree.root_node();
544:         self.traverse_for_growth(&root, source, false, &mut diags);
545:         diags
546:     }
547: 
548:     /// Recursive traversal looking for growth patterns inside loops.
549:     fn traverse_for_growth(
550:         &self,
551:         node: &tree_sitter::Node,
552:         source: &str,
553:         in_loop: bool,
554:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
555:     ) {
556:         let kind = node.kind();
557:         let entering_loop = kind == "for_statement" || kind == "while_statement";
558:         let now_in_loop = in_loop || entering_loop;
559: 
560:         // Only check assignment nodes inside loops.
561:         if now_in_loop && kind == "assignment" {
562:             self.check_assignment_growth(*node, source, diags);
563:         }
564: 
565:         // Also detect growth via full-node text for assignments that tree-sitter
566:         // may parse differently (e.g., s.field(end+1) = k might parse as
567:         // a function_call at statement level rather than an assignment).
568:         if now_in_loop
569:             && (kind == "function_call" || kind == "cell_index")
570:             && is_statement_level(node)
571:         {
572:             let text = node_text(*node, source);
573:             let normalized: String = text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
574:             if normalized.contains("end+1") {
575:                 let has_dot = text.contains('.');
576:                 let check_id = if has_dot { "SAGROW" } else { "AGROW" };
577:                 if self.is_enabled(check_id) {
578:                     diags.push(make_diag(check_id, *node));
579:                 }
580:             }
581:         }
582: 
583:         let count = node.child_count();
584:         for i in 0..count {
585:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
586:                 self.traverse_for_growth(&child, source, now_in_loop, diags);
587:             }
588:         }
589:     }

591:     /// Check a single assignment node for growth patterns.
592:     ///
593:     /// Detects:
594:     /// 1. `x = [x, val]` or `x = [x; val]` — concatenation growth (AGROW)
595:     /// 2. `x(end+1) = val` — end+1 indexing (AGROW)
596:     /// 3. `x{end+1} = val` — cell growth (AGROW)
597:     /// 4. `s.field(end+1) = val` — struct field growth (SAGROW)
598:     /// 5. `x = []` followed by growth — PFBNS (simplified: flag end+1 patterns)
599:     fn check_assignment_growth(
600:         &self,
601:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
602:         source: &str,
603:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
604:     ) {
605:         let lhs = match node.child_by_field_name("left").or_else(|| node.child(0)) {
606:             Some(n) => n,
607:             None => return,
608:         };
609:         let rhs = match node.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| node.child(2)) {
610:             Some(n) => n,
611:             None => return,
612:         };
613: 
614:         let lhs_text = node_text(lhs, source);
615:         let rhs_text = node_text(rhs, source);
616: 
617:         // Determine if LHS involves a struct field (for SAGROW vs AGROW).
618:         let is_struct = lhs.kind() == "field_expression"
619:             || (lhs.kind() == "function_call" && lhs_text.contains('.'));
620: 
621:         let check_id = if is_struct { "SAGROW" } else { "AGROW" };
622: 
623:         if !self.is_enabled(check_id) {
624:             return;
625:         }
626: 
627:         // Pattern 1: x(end+1) = ... or x{end+1} = ...
628:         // LHS is a function_call (indexing) or cell_index containing "end+1"
629:         // or "end + 1".
630:         if (lhs.kind() == "function_call" || lhs.kind() == "cell_index")
631:             && contains_end_plus_pattern(lhs, source)
632:         {
633:             diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
634:             return;
635:         }
636: 
637:         // Pattern 1b: s.field(end+1) = ... — may parse with field_expression as LHS
638:         // and end+1 in the assignment text before the `=`.
639:         if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
640:             // Check the full assignment text up to the `=` for end+1 pattern.
641:             let assign_text = node_text(node, source);
642:             if let Some(eq_pos) = assign_text.find('=') {
643:                 let lhs_full = &assign_text[..eq_pos];
644:                 let normalized: String = lhs_full.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
645:                 if normalized.contains("end+1") {
646:                     diags.push(make_diag("SAGROW", node));
647:                     return;
648:                 }
649:             }
650:         }
651: 
652:         // Pattern 2: x = [x, val] or x = [x; val]
653:         // LHS is a simple identifier, RHS is a matrix containing that identifier.
654:         if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
655:             let var_name = lhs_text;
656:             if rhs.kind() == "matrix" && matrix_contains_var(rhs, source, var_name) {
657:                 diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
658:                 return;
659:             }
660:             // Also check cell: x = {x, val} — though less common
661:             if rhs.kind() == "cell" && matrix_contains_var(rhs, source, var_name) {
662:                 diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
663:                 return;
664:             }
665:         }
666: 
667:         // Pattern 3: s.field = [s.field, val]
668:         if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
669:             let field_text = lhs_text;
670:             if rhs.kind() == "matrix" && rhs_text.contains(field_text) {
671:                 diags.push(make_diag("SAGROW", node));
672:             }
673:         }
674:     }
675: }

764: // Helper: node text extraction

766: 
767: /// Extract the raw text of a node.
768: fn node_text<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
769:     &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
770: }
771: 
772: /// Extract function name from a `function_call` node.
773: fn extract_func_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
774:     if node.kind() != "function_call" {
775:         return None;
776:     }
777:     let name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
778:     Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
779: }
780: 
781: /// Extract command name from a `command` node.
782: fn extract_command_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
783:     if node.kind() != "command" {
784:         return None;
785:     }
786:     let name_node = node.child(0)?;
787:     if name_node.kind() == "command_name" {
788:         Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
789:     } else {
790:         None
791:     }
792: }
793: 
794: /// Extract command arguments as a list of text fragments.
795: fn extract_command_args<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Vec<&'a str> {
796:     let mut args = Vec::new();
797:     let count = node.child_count();
798:     for i in 0..count {
799:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
800:             // Skip the command_name (first child) and punctuation.
801:             if child.kind() == "command_name" || child.kind() == ";" || child.kind() == "," {
802:                 continue;
803:             }
804:             let text = node_text(child, source).trim();
805:             if !text.is_empty() {
806:                 args.push(text);
807:             }
808:         }
809:     }
810:     args
811: }
812: 
813: /// Extract the operator text from a `binary_operator` or `boolean_operator`.
814: fn extract_operator<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
815:     // The operator is typically the second child (between left and right operands),
816:     // or we can scan children for the operator token.
817:     let count = node.child_count();
818:     for i in 0..count {
819:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
820:             let text = node_text(child, source);
821:             // Operator tokens are short and not identifiers/expressions.
822:             match text {
823:                 "+" | "-" | "*" | "/" | "\\" | "^" | ".*" | "./" | ".\\" | ".^" | "&" | "|"
824:                 | "&&" | "||" | "==" | "~=" | "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">=" => return text,
825:                 _ => continue,
826:             }
827:         }
828:     }
829:     ""
830: }
831: 
832: /// Extract the operator text from a `unary_operator` node.
833: fn extract_unary_operator<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
834:     if let Some(child) = node.child(0) {
835:         let text = node_text(child, source);
836:         match text {
837:             "~" | "-" | "+" | "!" => return text,
838:             _ => {}
839:         }
840:     }
841:     ""
842: }

844: /// Get the first named child of a node.
845: fn first_named_child(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node> {
846:     let count = node.named_child_count();
847:     if count > 0 {
848:         node.named_child(0)
849:     } else {
850:         None
851:     }
852: }

858: /// Count the number of arguments in a `function_call` node.
859: fn count_args(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> usize {
860:     // Arguments are in the `arguments` child node.
861:     match find_arguments(node) {
862:         Some(args_node) => args_node.named_child_count(),
863:         None => 0,
864:     }
865: }
866: 
867: /// Find the `arguments` child node of a `function_call` node.
868: ///
869: /// tree-sitter-matlab does not attach a field name to this child, so the
870: /// arguments list is located by node kind.
871: fn find_arguments<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node<'a>> {
872:     let count = node.child_count();
873:     for i in 0..count {
874:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
875:             if child.kind() == "arguments" {
876:                 return Some(child);
877:             }
878:         }
879:     }
880:     None
881: }

883: /// Check if a function_call has a specific string argument.
884: fn has_string_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str, value: &str) -> bool {
885:     let count = node.child_count();
886:     for i in 0..count {
887:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
888:             let text = node_text(child, source);
889:             // Match quoted strings: 'value' or "value"
890:             let trimmed = text.trim_matches('\'').trim_matches('"');
891:             if trimmed.eq_ignore_ascii_case(value) {
892:                 return true;
893:             }
894:             // Recurse into arguments node.
895:             if child.kind() == "arguments" && has_string_arg(child, source, value) {
896:                 return true;
897:             }
898:         }
899:     }
900:     false
901: }

903: /// Check if `exist(...)` has a second argument indicating type ('file', 'dir', etc.).
904: fn has_exist_type_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
905:     // exist should have 2 arguments, with the second being a string like 'file', 'dir'.
906:     let arg_count = count_args(node);
907:     if arg_count < 2 {
908:         return false;
909:     }
910:     has_string_arg(node, source, "file")
911:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "dir")
912:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "builtin")
913:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "class")
914: }

916: /// Check if a regexp/regexpi call has an overly simple pattern (just alphanumeric).
917: fn has_simple_regex_pattern(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
918:     // Look for the second argument (the pattern) and check if it's purely alphanumeric
919:     // (meaning a simple `contains` or `strcmp` would suffice).
920:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
921:         Some(n) => n,
922:         None => return false,
923:     };
924: 
925:     // The pattern is usually the 2nd argument.
926:     let named_count = args_node.named_child_count();
927:     if named_count < 2 {
928:         return false;
929:     }
930: 
931:     if let Some(pattern_node) = args_node.named_child(1) {
932:         let text = node_text(pattern_node, source);
933:         // Strip quotes.
934:         let inner = text.trim_matches('\'').trim_matches('"');
935:         // If the pattern is purely alphanumeric (no regex metacharacters), it's simple.
936:         if !inner.is_empty() && inner.chars().all(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_') {
937:             return true;
938:         }
939:     }
940:     false
941: }

943: /// Check if the first argument to lower/upper is a strcmp call (STNCI pattern).
944: fn has_strcmp_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
945:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
946:         Some(n) => n,
947:         None => return false,
948:     };
949: 
950:     if let Some(first_arg) = first_named_child(args_node) {
951:         if first_arg.kind() == "function_call" {
952:             if let Some(name) = extract_func_name(first_arg, source) {
953:                 return name == "strcmp" || name == "strcmpi";
954:             }
955:         }
956:     }
957:     false
958: }

964: /// Check if the function_call is a nested call of the same function.
965: /// e.g., max(max(x)) — the outer call's first argument is the same function.
966: fn is_nested_same_call(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str, func_name: &str) -> bool {
967:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
968:         Some(n) => n,
969:         None => return false,
970:     };
971: 
972:     // Check if first argument is a function_call with the same name.
973:     if let Some(first_arg) = first_named_child(args_node) {
974:         if first_arg.kind() == "function_call" {
975:             if let Some(inner_name) = extract_func_name(first_arg, source) {
976:                 return inner_name == func_name;
977:             }
978:         }
979:     }
980:     false
981: }

983: /// Check if a function_call node is used as a subscript index.
984: /// i.e., the parent is the arguments of another function_call.
985: fn is_subscript_context(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
986:     if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
987:         // Direct parent might be `arguments` of a function_call.
988:         if parent.kind() == "arguments" {
989:             if let Some(grandparent) = parent.parent() {
990:                 return grandparent.kind() == "function_call";
991:             }
992:         }
993:         // Or the parent is directly a function_call (as an argument).
994:         if parent.kind() == "function_call" {
995:             // Make sure this node is not the function name itself.
996:             if let Some(name_node) = parent.child_by_field_name("name") {
997:                 return name_node.id() != node.id();
998:             }
999:         }
1000:     }
1001:     false
1002: }

1004: /// Check if a node is at statement level (direct child of source_file or block).
1005: fn is_statement_level(node: &tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
1006:     node.parent()
1007:         .map(|p| matches!(p.kind(), "source_file" | "block"))
1008:         .unwrap_or(false)
1009: }

1011: /// Check if node is inside a loop (for_statement or while_statement).
1012: fn is_inside_loop(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
1013:     let mut current = node.parent();
1014:     while let Some(p) = current {
1015:         match p.kind() {
1016:             "for_statement" | "while_statement" => return true,
1017:             "function_definition" => return false, // Stop at function boundary.
1018:             _ => {}
1019:         }
1020:         current = p.parent();
1021:     }
1022:     false
1023: }
1024: 
1025: /// Check if a node is inside a condition expression (if/while/elseif).
1026: fn is_in_condition(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
1027:     let mut current = node.parent();
1028:     while let Some(p) = current {
1029:         match p.kind() {
1030:             "if_statement" | "while_statement" | "elseif_clause" => {
1031:                 // Check if our node is in the condition part, not the body.
1032:                 // The condition is typically the first expression child after the keyword.
1033:                 if let Some(cond) = p.child_by_field_name("condition") {
1034:                     return is_descendant_of(node, cond);
1035:                 }
1036:                 // Fallback: check if node appears before the "block" child.
1037:                 let count = p.child_count();
1038:                 for i in 0..count {
1039:                     if let Some(child) = p.child(i) {
1040:                         if child.kind() == "block" {
1041:                             // If node is before the block, it's in the condition.
1042:                             return node.start_byte() < child.start_byte();
1043:                         }
1044:                     }
1045:                 }
1046:                 return true;
1047:             }
1048:             "function_definition" => return false,
1049:             _ => {}
1050:         }
1051:         current = p.parent();
1052:     }
1053:     false
1054: }

1056: /// Check if `needle` is a descendant of `haystack`.
1057: fn is_descendant_of(needle: tree_sitter::Node, haystack: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
1058:     needle.start_byte() >= haystack.start_byte() && needle.end_byte() <= haystack.end_byte()
1059: }

1061: /// Check if an `inv()` call is an operand of a binary_operator.
1062: fn has_inv_operand(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
1063:     let count = node.child_count();
1064:     for i in 0..count {
1065:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
1066:             if child.kind() == "function_call" {
1067:                 if let Some(name) = extract_func_name(child, source) {
1068:                     if name == "inv" {
1069:                         return true;
1070:                     }
1071:                 }
1072:             }
1073:         }
1074:     }
1075:     false
1076: }

1078: /// Check if both operands of a binary_operator are the same text.
1079: fn has_same_operands(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
1080:     // Typically: child(0) = left, child(1) = op, child(2) = right.
1081:     let left = match node.child(0) {
1082:         Some(n) => n,
1083:         None => return false,
1084:     };
1085:     let right = match node.child(2) {
1086:         Some(n) => n,
1087:         None => return false,
1088:     };
1089:     let left_text = node_text(left, source).trim();
1090:     let right_text = node_text(right, source).trim();
1091:     !left_text.is_empty() && left_text == right_text
1092: }

31: /// the Linter's depth-first dispatch. Returns all diagnostics.
32: pub fn lint_nodes(rule: &dyn Rule, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
33:     let tree = parse(source);
34:     let path = std::path::Path::new("test.m");
35:     let targets: Vec<&str> = rule.target_node_types().to_vec();
36:     let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();

38:     fn walk(
39:         node: Node,
40:         source: &str,
41:         path: &std::path::Path,
42:         targets: &[&str],
43:         rule: &dyn Rule,
44:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
45:     ) {
46:         if targets.contains(&node.kind()) {
47:             let ctx = NodeContext {
48:                 node,
49:                 source,
50:                 file_path: path,
51:             };
52:             diagnostics.extend(rule.check(&ctx));
53:         }

56:             walk(child, source, path, targets, rule, diagnostics);

141: /// Hybrid performance engine covering 41 performance checks.
142: ///
143: /// Node-level checks fire on `function_call`, `command`, `binary_operator`,
144: /// `boolean_operator`, and `comparison_operator`. File-level checks (AGROW,
145: /// SAGROW, PFBNS) traverse the full tree for loop growth patterns.
146: pub struct PerformanceEngine {
147:     config: PerformanceEngineConfig,
148: }
149: 
150: /// Node types for node-level dispatch.
151: const TARGET_NODES: &[&str] = &[
152:     "function_call",
153:     "command",
154:     "binary_operator",
155:     "boolean_operator",
156:     "comparison_operator",
157:     "unary_operator",
158: ];

160: impl PerformanceEngine {
161:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
162:         let rule_config: PerformanceEngineConfig = config.rule_params("PERFORMANCE_ENGINE");
163:         Box::new(Self {
164:             config: rule_config,
165:         })
166:     }
167:     fn is_enabled(&self, check_id: &str) -> bool {
168:         !self.config.skip_checks.iter().any(|s| s == check_id)
169:     }
170: 
171:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
172:     // File-level checks: AGROW, SAGROW, PFBNS
173:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
174: 
175:     fn check_growth_in_loops(
176:         &self,
177:         tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
178:         source: &str,
179:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
180:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
181:         let root = tree.root_node();
182:         self.traverse_for_growth(&root, source, false, &mut diags);
183:         diags
184:     }
185:     fn traverse_for_growth(
186:         &self,
187:         node: &tree_sitter::Node,
188:         source: &str,
189:         in_loop: bool,
190:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
191:     ) {
192:         let kind = node.kind();
193:         let entering_loop = kind == "for_statement" || kind == "while_statement";
194:         let now_in_loop = in_loop || entering_loop;
195: 
196:         // Only check assignment nodes inside loops.
197:         if now_in_loop && kind == "assignment" {
198:             self.check_assignment_growth(*node, source, diags);
199:         }
200: 
201:         // Also detect growth via full-node text for assignments that tree-sitter
202:         // may parse differently (e.g., s.field(end+1) = k might parse as
203:         // a function_call at statement level rather than an assignment).
204:         if now_in_loop
205:             && (kind == "function_call" || kind == "cell_index")
206:             && is_statement_level(node)
207:         {
208:             let text = node_text(*node, source);
209:             let normalized: String = text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
210:             if normalized.contains("end+1") {
211:                 let has_dot = text.contains('.');
212:                 let check_id = if has_dot { "SAGROW" } else { "AGROW" };
213:                 if self.is_enabled(check_id) {
214:                     diags.push(make_diag(check_id, *node));
215:                 }
216:             }
217:         }
218: 
219:         let count = node.child_count();
220:         for i in 0..count {
221:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
222:                 self.traverse_for_growth(&child, source, now_in_loop, diags);
223:             }
224:         }
225:     }
226:     fn check_assignment_growth(
227:         &self,
228:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
229:         source: &str,
230:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
231:     ) {
232:         let lhs = match node.child_by_field_name("left").or_else(|| node.child(0)) {
233:             Some(n) => n,
234:             None => return,
235:         };
236:         let rhs = match node.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| node.child(2)) {
237:             Some(n) => n,
238:             None => return,
239:         };
240: 
241:         let lhs_text = node_text(lhs, source);
242:         let rhs_text = node_text(rhs, source);
243: 
244:         // Determine if LHS involves a struct field (for SAGROW vs AGROW).
245:         let is_struct = lhs.kind() == "field_expression"
246:             || (lhs.kind() == "function_call" && lhs_text.contains('.'));
247: 
248:         let check_id = if is_struct { "SAGROW" } else { "AGROW" };
249: 
250:         if !self.is_enabled(check_id) {
251:             return;
252:         }
253: 
254:         // Pattern 1: x(end+1) = ... or x{end+1} = ...
255:         // LHS is a function_call (indexing) or cell_index containing "end+1"
256:         // or "end + 1".
257:         if (lhs.kind() == "function_call" || lhs.kind() == "cell_index")
258:             && contains_end_plus_pattern(lhs, source)
259:         {
260:             diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
261:             return;
262:         }
263: 
264:         // Pattern 1b: s.field(end+1) = ... — may parse with field_expression as LHS
265:         // and end+1 in the assignment text before the `=`.
266:         if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
267:             // Check the full assignment text up to the `=` for end+1 pattern.
268:             let assign_text = node_text(node, source);
269:             if let Some(eq_pos) = assign_text.find('=') {
270:                 let lhs_full = &assign_text[..eq_pos];
271:                 let normalized: String = lhs_full.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
272:                 if normalized.contains("end+1") {
273:                     diags.push(make_diag("SAGROW", node));
274:                     return;
275:                 }
276:             }
277:         }
278: 
279:         // Pattern 2: x = [x, val] or x = [x; val]
280:         // LHS is a simple identifier, RHS is a matrix containing that identifier.
281:         if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
282:             let var_name = lhs_text;
283:             if rhs.kind() == "matrix" && matrix_contains_var(rhs, source, var_name) {
284:                 diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
285:                 return;
286:             }
287:             // Also check cell: x = {x, val} — though less common
288:             if rhs.kind() == "cell" && matrix_contains_var(rhs, source, var_name) {
289:                 diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
290:                 return;
291:             }
292:         }
293: 
294:         // Pattern 3: s.field = [s.field, val]
295:         if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
296:             let field_text = lhs_text;
297:             if rhs.kind() == "matrix" && rhs_text.contains(field_text) {
298:                 diags.push(make_diag("SAGROW", node));
299:             }
300:         }
301:     }
302: }

331:             "function_call" => self.check_function_call(ctx.node, ctx.source),
332:             "command" => self.check_command(ctx.node, ctx.source),
333:             "binary_operator" => {
334:                 let mut diags = self.check_binary_operator(ctx.node, ctx.source);

336:                 diags.extend(self.check_boolean_context_binary(ctx.node, ctx.source));

341:                 Vec::new()
342:             }
343:             "comparison_operator" => self.check_comparison(ctx.node, ctx.source),
344:             "unary_operator" => self.check_unary(ctx.node, ctx.source),
345:             _ => Vec::new(),
346:         }
347:     }

350:         self.check_growth_in_loops(ctx.tree, ctx.source)
351:     }

371:     check_id: &'static str,

386: pub(crate) fn node_text<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
387:     &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
388: }
389: pub(crate) fn extract_func_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
390:     if node.kind() != "function_call" {
391:         return None;
392:     }
393:     let name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
394:     Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
395: }
396: pub(crate) fn extract_command_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
397:     if node.kind() != "command" {
398:         return None;
399:     }
400:     let name_node = node.child(0)?;
401:     if name_node.kind() == "command_name" {
402:         Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
403:     } else {
404:         None
405:     }
406: }
407: pub(crate) fn extract_command_args<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Vec<&'a str> {
408:     let mut args = Vec::new();
409:     let count = node.child_count();
410:     for i in 0..count {
411:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
412:             // Skip the command_name (first child) and punctuation.
413:             if child.kind() == "command_name" || child.kind() == ";" || child.kind() == "," {
414:                 continue;
415:             }
416:             let text = node_text(child, source).trim();
417:             if !text.is_empty() {
418:                 args.push(text);
419:             }
420:         }
421:     }
422:     args
423: }
424: pub(crate) fn extract_operator<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
425:     // The operator is typically the second child (between left and right operands),
426:     // or we can scan children for the operator token.
427:     let count = node.child_count();
428:     for i in 0..count {
429:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
430:             let text = node_text(child, source);
431:             // Operator tokens are short and not identifiers/expressions.
432:             match text {
433:                 "+" | "-" | "*" | "/" | "\\" | "^" | ".*" | "./" | ".\\" | ".^" | "&" | "|"
434:                 | "&&" | "||" | "==" | "~=" | "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">=" => return text,
435:                 _ => continue,
436:             }
437:         }
438:     }
439:     ""
440: }
441: pub(crate) fn extract_unary_operator<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
442:     if let Some(child) = node.child(0) {
443:         let text = node_text(child, source);
444:         match text {
445:             "~" | "-" | "+" | "!" => return text,
446:             _ => {}
447:         }
448:     }
449:     ""
450: }
451: pub(crate) fn first_named_child(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node> {
452:     let count = node.named_child_count();
453:     if count > 0 {
454:         node.named_child(0)
455:     } else {
456:         None
457:     }
458: }
459: pub(crate) fn count_args(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> usize {
460:     // Arguments are in the `arguments` child node.
461:     match find_arguments(node) {
462:         Some(args_node) => args_node.named_child_count(),
463:         None => 0,
464:     }
465: }
466: pub(crate) fn find_arguments<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node<'a>> {
467:     let count = node.child_count();
468:     for i in 0..count {
469:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
470:             if child.kind() == "arguments" {
471:                 return Some(child);
472:             }
473:         }
474:     }
475:     None
476: }
477: pub(crate) fn has_string_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str, value: &str) -> bool {
478:     let count = node.child_count();
479:     for i in 0..count {
480:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
481:             let text = node_text(child, source);
482:             // Match quoted strings: 'value' or "value"
483:             let trimmed = text.trim_matches('\'').trim_matches('"');
484:             if trimmed.eq_ignore_ascii_case(value) {
485:                 return true;
486:             }
487:             // Recurse into arguments node.
488:             if child.kind() == "arguments" && has_string_arg(child, source, value) {
489:                 return true;
490:             }
491:         }
492:     }
493:     false
494: }
495: pub(crate) fn has_exist_type_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
496:     // exist should have 2 arguments, with the second being a string like 'file', 'dir'.
497:     let arg_count = count_args(node);
498:     if arg_count < 2 {
499:         return false;
500:     }
501:     has_string_arg(node, source, "file")
502:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "dir")
503:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "builtin")
504:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "class")
505: }
506: pub(crate) fn has_simple_regex_pattern(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
507:     // Look for the second argument (the pattern) and check if it's purely alphanumeric
508:     // (meaning a simple `contains` or `strcmp` would suffice).
509:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
510:         Some(n) => n,
511:         None => return false,
512:     };
513: 
514:     // The pattern is usually the 2nd argument.
515:     let named_count = args_node.named_child_count();
516:     if named_count < 2 {
517:         return false;
518:     }
519: 
520:     if let Some(pattern_node) = args_node.named_child(1) {
521:         let text = node_text(pattern_node, source);
522:         // Strip quotes.
523:         let inner = text.trim_matches('\'').trim_matches('"');
524:         // If the pattern is purely alphanumeric (no regex metacharacters), it's simple.
525:         if !inner.is_empty() && inner.chars().all(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_') {
526:             return true;
527:         }
528:     }
529:     false
530: }
531: pub(crate) fn has_strcmp_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
532:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
533:         Some(n) => n,
534:         None => return false,
535:     };
536: 
537:     if let Some(first_arg) = first_named_child(args_node) {
538:         if first_arg.kind() == "function_call" {
539:             if let Some(name) = extract_func_name(first_arg, source) {
540:                 return name == "strcmp" || name == "strcmpi";
541:             }
542:         }
543:     }
544:     false
545: }
546: pub(crate) fn is_nested_same_call(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str, func_name: &str) -> bool {
547:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
548:         Some(n) => n,
549:         None => return false,
550:     };
551: 
552:     // Check if first argument is a function_call with the same name.
553:     if let Some(first_arg) = first_named_child(args_node) {
554:         if first_arg.kind() == "function_call" {
555:             if let Some(inner_name) = extract_func_name(first_arg, source) {
556:                 return inner_name == func_name;
557:             }
558:         }
559:     }
560:     false
561: }
562: pub(crate) fn is_subscript_context(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
563:     if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
564:         // Direct parent might be `arguments` of a function_call.
565:         if parent.kind() == "arguments" {
566:             if let Some(grandparent) = parent.parent() {
567:                 return grandparent.kind() == "function_call";
568:             }
569:         }
570:         // Or the parent is directly a function_call (as an argument).
571:         if parent.kind() == "function_call" {
572:             // Make sure this node is not the function name itself.
573:             if let Some(name_node) = parent.child_by_field_name("name") {
574:                 return name_node.id() != node.id();
575:             }
576:         }
577:     }
578:     false
579: }
580: pub(crate) fn is_statement_level(node: &tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
581:     node.parent()
582:         .map(|p| matches!(p.kind(), "source_file" | "block"))
583:         .unwrap_or(false)
584: }
585: pub(crate) fn is_inside_loop(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
586:     let mut current = node.parent();
587:     while let Some(p) = current {
588:         match p.kind() {
589:             "for_statement" | "while_statement" => return true,
590:             "function_definition" => return false, // Stop at function boundary.
